################################################################################
# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/assistant/Assistant.kt
################################################################################
package com.example.retrodatabases.assistant

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.DatabaseEntity
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/**
 * The on-device helper for the catalogue. It decides what a question asks for (see [IntentClassifier]), reads the
 * database number, the years and the kind out of the words, looks the records up in a [RecordIndex] and writes a
 * short answer. Everything runs on the phone: no question leaves the device.
 */
class Assistant(
    private val databases: List<DatabaseEntity>,
    private val records: List<RecordEntity>,
    private val years: Map<Long, IntRange>,
    private val classifier: IntentClassifier = IntentClassifier(),
) {

    /** What was understood, the text to show, and the records to offer. */
    data class Answer(val intent: Intent, val text: String, val hits: List<RecordIndex.Hit>)

    private val index: RecordIndex by lazy { RecordIndex(records) }
    private val databaseById: Map<Long, DatabaseEntity> = databases.associateBy { it.id }
    private val countByDatabase: Map<Long, Int> = records.groupingBy { it.databaseId }.eachCount()
    private val countByKind: Map<Kind, Int> = records.groupingBy { it.kind }.eachCount()
    private val rareCount: Int = records.count { it.rare }

    /** Answers one question. The answer is in Russian when the question has Cyrillic letters, otherwise in English. */
    fun answer(question: String): Answer {
        val russian = question.any { it in 'Ѐ'..'ӿ' }
        val (guess, confidence) = classifier.classify(question)
        val intent = when {
            startsWithSearchVerb(question) -> Intent.FIND
            confidence < MIN_CONFIDENCE -> Intent.UNKNOWN
            else -> guess
        }
        val slots = Slots.parse(question, databaseById.keys)
        return when (intent) {
            Intent.FIND -> find(question, slots, russian, fallback = false)
            Intent.DATABASES -> listDatabases(russian)
            Intent.COVERAGE -> coverage(slots, russian)
            Intent.RUNNABLE -> runnable(question, slots, russian)
            Intent.APP_HELP -> Answer(Intent.APP_HELP, if (russian) HELP_RU else HELP_EN, emptyList())
            Intent.STATS -> stats(slots, russian)
            Intent.UNKNOWN -> find(question, slots, russian, fallback = true)
        }
    }

    /**
     * A question that opens with a search verb asks for records, even when it names a database or a year. The
     * exception is a question about how to search: one that contains "how" or "как" goes to the classifier.
     */
    private fun startsWithSearchVerb(question: String): Boolean {
        val tokens = Tokenizer.tokens(question)
        val first = tokens.firstOrNull() ?: return false
        return first in SEARCH_VERBS && tokens.none { it in HOW_WORDS }
    }

    private fun find(question: String, slots: Slots, russian: Boolean, fallback: Boolean): Answer {
        val hits = index.search(question, limit = SEARCH_POOL)
            .filter { slots.matches(it.record) }
            .take(MAX_HITS)
        if (hits.isEmpty()) {
            val text = when {
                fallback && russian -> NOT_UNDERSTOOD_RU
                fallback -> NOT_UNDERSTOOD_EN
                russian -> NOTHING_FOUND_RU
                else -> NOTHING_FOUND_EN
            }
            return Answer(if (fallback) Intent.UNKNOWN else Intent.FIND, text, emptyList())
        }
        return Answer(Intent.FIND, if (russian) BEST_MATCHES_RU else BEST_MATCHES_EN, hits)
    }

    private fun listDatabases(russian: Boolean): Answer {
        val shown = databases.sortedBy { it.id }.take(LIST_LIMIT)
        val lines = shown.joinToString("\n") { db ->
            "Database ${db.id}: ${yearsText(db.id, russian)}, ${countByDatabase[db.id] ?: 0} records"
        }
        val rest = databases.size - shown.size
        val first = databases.minOfOrNull { it.id } ?: 0L
        val last = databases.maxOfOrNull { it.id } ?: 0L
        val head = if (russian) {
            "Всего баз: ${databases.size}, номера с $first по $last."
        } else {
            "There are ${databases.size} databases, numbered $first to $last."
        }
        val tail = when {
            rest <= 0 -> ""
            russian -> "\nи ещё $rest. Все базы перечислены на первом экране."
            else -> "\nand $rest more. The Databases screen lists them all."
        }
        return Answer(Intent.DATABASES, "$head\n$lines$tail", emptyList())
    }

    private fun coverage(slots: Slots, russian: Boolean): Answer {
        slots.databaseId?.let { id ->
            val name = databaseById.getValue(id).name
            val text = if (russian) {
                "База $id ($name) охватывает ${yearsText(id, true)} и содержит ${countByDatabase[id] ?: 0} записей."
            } else {
                "Database $id ($name) covers ${yearsText(id, false)} and has ${countByDatabase[id] ?: 0} records."
            }
            return Answer(Intent.COVERAGE, text, emptyList())
        }
        val wanted = slots.years ?: return Answer(
            Intent.COVERAGE,
            if (russian) ASK_NUMBER_RU else ASK_NUMBER_EN,
            emptyList(),
        )
        val matching = databases
            .filter { db -> yearsOf(db.id).let { range -> range.first <= wanted.last && wanted.first <= range.last } }
            .map { it.id }
            .sorted()
        val text = when {
            matching.isEmpty() && russian -> "Ни одна база не охватывает эти годы."
            matching.isEmpty() -> "No database covers those years."
            russian -> "Эти годы охватывают базы: ${matching.joinToString(", ")}."
            else -> "Those years are covered by database ${matching.joinToString(", ")}."
        }
        return Answer(Intent.COVERAGE, text, emptyList())
    }

    private fun runnable(question: String, slots: Slots, russian: Boolean): Answer {
        val scores = index.search(question, limit = records.size).associate { it.doc to it.score }
        val pool = records.indices.filter { doc ->
            val record = records[doc]
            record.kind in RUNNABLE_KINDS && record.example != null && slots.matches(record)
        }
        if (pool.isEmpty()) {
            return Answer(Intent.RUNNABLE, if (russian) NO_RUNNABLE_RU else NO_RUNNABLE_EN, emptyList())
        }
        val hits = pool
            .sortedWith(compareByDescending<Int> { scores[it] ?: 0.0 }.thenBy { records[it].title })
            .take(MAX_HITS)
            .map { RecordIndex.Hit(records[it], scores[it] ?: 0.0, it) }
        val text = if (russian) {
            "Записей с кодом для запуска: ${pool.size}. Вот первые ${hits.size}."
        } else {
            "Runnable records: ${pool.size}. The first ${hits.size} are below."
        }
        return Answer(Intent.RUNNABLE, text, hits)
    }

    private fun stats(slots: Slots, russian: Boolean): Answer {
        val id = slots.databaseId
        if (id != null) {
            val rare = records.count { it.databaseId == id && it.rare }
            val text = if (russian) {
                "База $id: записей ${countByDatabase[id] ?: 0}, из них редких $rare."
            } else {
                "Database $id has ${countByDatabase[id] ?: 0} records, $rare of them rare."
            }
            return Answer(Intent.STATS, text, emptyList())
        }
        val byKind = Kind.entries.joinToString(", ") { "${kindLabel(it, russian)} ${countByKind[it] ?: 0}" }
        val text = if (russian) {
            "В каталоге ${records.size} записей в ${databases.size} базах, редких: $rareCount. По видам: $byKind."
        } else {
            "The catalogue has ${records.size} records in ${databases.size} databases; $rareCount are rare. By kind: $byKind."
        }
        return Answer(Intent.STATS, text, emptyList())
    }

    /** The years of a database: its declared range, or the years of its records when none is declared. */
    private fun yearsOf(id: Long): IntRange = years[id] ?: records
        .filter { it.databaseId == id }
        .map { it.year }
        .let { all -> if (all.isEmpty()) 0..0 else all.min()..all.max() }

    private fun yearsText(id: Long, russian: Boolean): String {
        val range = yearsOf(id)
        return if (russian) "годы ${range.first}–${range.last}" else "years ${range.first} to ${range.last}"
    }

    private fun kindLabel(kind: Kind, russian: Boolean): String = if (!russian) kind.label else when (kind) {
        Kind.LANGUAGE -> "Языки"
        Kind.SYSTEM -> "Системы"
        Kind.DEVICE -> "Устройства"
        Kind.TOOL -> "Инструменты"
        Kind.PRACTICE -> "Практики"
        Kind.GUIDE -> "Руководства"
        Kind.EXAMPLE -> "Примеры"
        Kind.PROJECT -> "Проекты"
        Kind.FLEX -> "Flex"
        Kind.CROSS -> "Cross-code"
        Kind.MODEL -> "Экономические модели"
        Kind.COMPROMISE -> "Компромиссы"
    }

    /** The database number, the years and the kind that a question names. Each one is optional. */
    private class Slots(val databaseId: Long?, val years: IntRange?, val kind: Kind?) {

        fun matches(record: RecordEntity): Boolean =
            (databaseId == null || record.databaseId == databaseId) &&
                (years == null || record.year in years) &&
                (kind == null || record.kind == kind)

        companion object {
            private val databaseNumber = Regex("(?:database|db|база|базы|базе|базу|бд)\\s*№?\\s*(\\d{1,3})")
            private val decade = Regex("\\b(\\d{3})0(?:s\\b|-\\p{L}+)")
            private val number = Regex("\\b(\\d{1,4})\\b")

            /** Kind words: each kind is recognised by the start of a word, so Russian endings still match. */
            private val kindStems: List<Pair<Kind, List<String>>> = listOf(
                Kind.LANGUAGE to listOf("language", "язык"),
                Kind.SYSTEM to listOf("system", "систем"),
                Kind.DEVICE to listOf("device", "устройств"),
                Kind.TOOL to listOf("tool", "инструмент"),
                Kind.PRACTICE to listOf("practice", "практик"),
                Kind.GUIDE to listOf("guide", "руковод", "инструкц"),
                Kind.EXAMPLE to listOf("example", "пример"),
                Kind.PROJECT to listOf("project", "проект"),
                Kind.FLEX to listOf("flex"),
                Kind.CROSS to listOf("cross"),
                Kind.MODEL to listOf("model", "модел", "econom", "экономи"),
                Kind.COMPROMISE to listOf("compromis", "компромисс"),
            )

            fun parse(question: String, databaseIds: Set<Long>): Slots {
                val text = question.lowercase().replace('ё', 'е')
                val named = databaseNumber.find(text)?.groupValues?.get(1)?.toLong()
                val databaseId = named?.takeIf { it in databaseIds }
                val years: IntRange? = decade.find(text)?.let { match ->
                    val start = match.groupValues[1].toInt() * 10
                    start..start + 9
                } ?: yearWords(text, named)
                val tokens = Tokenizer.tokens(question)
                val kind = kindStems.firstNotNullOfOrNull { (kind, stems) ->
                    kind.takeIf { tokens.any { token -> stems.any { token.startsWith(it) } } }
                }
                return Slots(databaseId, years, kind)
            }

            /**
             * A year is a number of three or four digits, or a shorter number after the word for year. Shorter numbers
             * on their own are usually something else (a chapter, a count) and are ignored.
             */
            private fun yearWords(text: String, named: Long?): IntRange? {
                val yearContext = text.contains("year") || text.contains("год")
                return number.findAll(text)
                    .map { it.groupValues[1] }
                    .filter { it.toLong() != named }
                    .filter { it.length >= 3 || yearContext }
                    .map { it.toInt() }
                    .firstOrNull { it in 0..2100 }
                    ?.let { it..it }
            }
        }
    }

    private companion object {
        const val MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.4

################################################################################
# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/assistant/IntentClassifier.kt
################################################################################
package com.example.retrodatabases.assistant

import kotlin.math.exp
import kotlin.math.ln

/** What the user wants from the assistant. */
enum class Intent { FIND, DATABASES, COVERAGE, RUNNABLE, APP_HELP, STATS, UNKNOWN }

/**
 * A multinomial naive Bayes classifier over word tokens. It is trained on the example questions in [TrainingExamples]
 * when it is created. It keeps only word counts in memory, and needs no network and no model file.
 */
class IntentClassifier(examples: List<Pair<Intent, String>> = TrainingExamples.all) {

    private val logPrior = HashMap<Intent, Double>()
    private val logLikelihood = HashMap<Intent, Map<String, Double>>()
    private val logUnseen = HashMap<Intent, Double>()
    private val vocabulary: Set<String>

    init {
        val counts = HashMap<Intent, HashMap<String, Int>>()
        val documents = HashMap<Intent, Int>()
        for ((intent, text) in examples) {
            documents[intent] = (documents[intent] ?: 0) + 1
            val bag = counts.getOrPut(intent) { HashMap() }
            for (token in Tokenizer.tokens(text)) bag[token] = (bag[token] ?: 0) + 1
        }
        vocabulary = counts.values.flatMapTo(HashSet()) { it.keys }
        val total = examples.size.toDouble()
        for ((intent, count) in documents) {
            logPrior[intent] = ln(count / total)
            val bag = counts.getValue(intent)
            // Laplace smoothing: every word of the vocabulary gets one extra count for every intent.
            val denominator = bag.values.sum() + vocabulary.size.toDouble()
            logLikelihood[intent] = bag.mapValues { (_, c) -> ln((c + 1) / denominator) }
            logUnseen[intent] = ln(1.0 / denominator)
        }
    }

    /**
     * The most likely intent and its probability among the intents (0 to 1). Words that the training set never saw
     * are ignored; a question made only of such words gets [Intent.UNKNOWN] with probability 0.
     */
    fun classify(text: String): Pair<Intent, Double> {
        val known = Tokenizer.tokens(text).filter { it in vocabulary }
        if (known.isEmpty()) return Intent.UNKNOWN to 0.0
        val scores = logPrior.mapValues { (intent, prior) ->
            val likelihood = logLikelihood.getValue(intent)
            val unseen = logUnseen.getValue(intent)
            prior + known.sumOf { token -> likelihood[token] ?: unseen }
        }
        val best = scores.maxByOrNull { it.value } ?: return Intent.UNKNOWN to 0.0
        val top = best.value
        val sum = scores.values.sumOf { exp(it - top) }
        return best.key to 1.0 / sum
    }
}

/** Example questions for each intent, in English and in Russian. */
object TrainingExamples {

################################################################################
# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/assistant/RecordIndex.kt
################################################################################
package com.example.retrodatabases.assistant

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity
import kotlin.math.ln

/**
 * A compact BM25 index over the catalogue records. Each field adds a weight to the terms it contains: the title counts
 * most, then the original title, the section and the year, then the author, the kind, the summary and last the details.
 * The index is built once from the records and only read afterwards, so it can be shared.
 */
class RecordIndex(private val records: List<RecordEntity>) {

    /** One matching record: its score (higher is better) and its position in the records list. */
    data class Hit(val record: RecordEntity, val score: Double, val doc: Int)

    /** The records that contain one term, with the weight of the term in each: two parallel arrays, no boxing. */
    private class Postings {
        var docs = IntArray(4)
        var weights = FloatArray(4)
        var size = 0

        fun add(doc: Int, weight: Float) {
            if (size == docs.size) {
                docs = docs.copyOf(size * 2)
                weights = weights.copyOf(size * 2)
            }
            docs[size] = doc
            weights[size] = weight
            size++
        }
    }

    private val postings = HashMap<String, Postings>()
    private val lengths = FloatArray(records.size)
    private val averageLength: Float

    init {
        records.forEachIndexed { doc, record ->
            val weights = HashMap<String, Float>()
            var length = 0f
            for ((text, fieldWeight) in fieldsOf(record)) {
                for (token in Tokenizer.contentTokens(text)) {
                    weights[token] = (weights[token] ?: 0f) + fieldWeight
                    length += fieldWeight
                }
            }
            lengths[doc] = length
            for ((token, weight) in weights) {
                postings.getOrPut(token) { Postings() }.add(doc, weight)
            }
        }
        averageLength = if (records.isEmpty()) 1f else lengths.average().toFloat().coerceAtLeast(1f)
    }

    /** Number of distinct terms in the index. */
    val termCount: Int get() = postings.size

    /** Number of term and record pairs in the index: a measure of its size. */
    val postingCount: Int get() = postings.values.sumOf { it.size }

    /** The records that match the query, best first. Records that share no term with the query are left out. */
    fun search(query: String, limit: Int = 10): List<Hit> {
        val terms = Tokenizer.contentTokens(query).distinct()
        if (terms.isEmpty() || records.isEmpty()) return emptyList()
        val scores = HashMap<Int, Double>()
        for (term in terms) {
            val list = postings[term] ?: continue
            val idf = ln(1.0 + (records.size - list.size + 0.5) / (list.size + 0.5))
            for (i in 0 until list.size) {
                val doc = list.docs[i]
                val tf = list.weights[i].toDouble()
                val normalised = K1 * (1.0 - B + B * (lengths[doc] / averageLength))
                scores[doc] = (scores[doc] ?: 0.0) + idf * tf * (K1 + 1.0) / (tf + normalised)
            }
        }
        return scores.entries
            .sortedWith(compareByDescending<Map.Entry<Int, Double>> { it.value }.thenBy { records[it.key].title })
            .take(limit)
            .map { Hit(records[it.key], it.value, it.key) }
    }

    private fun fieldsOf(record: RecordEntity): List<Pair<String, Float>> = listOf(
        record.title to 3f,
        record.originalTitle to 2f,
        record.section to 2f,
        record.year.toString() to 2f,
        record.author to 1.5f,
        record.kind.label to 1f,
        record.summary to 1f,
        record.details to 0.5f,
    )

    private companion object {
        const val K1 = 1.2
        const val B = 0.75
    }
}

################################################################################
# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/assistant/Tokenizer.kt
################################################################################
package com.example.retrodatabases.assistant

/**
 * Splits text into lowercase word tokens. Letters and digits of every script are kept, so English and Russian
 * questions go through the same code. The letter with diaeresis is folded into the plain letter, so both spellings match.
 */
object Tokenizer {

    private val separator = Regex("[^\\p{L}\\p{Nd}]+")

    /** Every token of the text, function words included. Used to recognise what a question asks for. */
    fun tokens(text: String): List<String> =
        text.lowercase()
            .replace('ё', 'е')
            .split(separator)
            .filter { it.isNotEmpty() }

    /** The tokens that carry the subject of a question: function words and one-letter tokens are dropped. */
    fun contentTokens(text: String): List<String> =
        tokens(text).filter { it.length > 1 && it !in stopWords }

    /** Function words and request words in English and Russian. They are too frequent to help a search. */
    private val stopWords: Set<String> = setOf(
        "a", "an", "and", "are", "as", "at", "be", "by", "can", "could", "do", "does", "find", "for", "from", "give",
        "how", "i", "in", "is", "it", "list", "me", "my", "of", "on", "or", "search", "show", "tell", "the", "to",
        "what", "where", "which", "who", "with", "you", "your", "there",
        "и", "в", "во", "не", "на", "что", "как", "где", "какой", "какая", "какие", "каких", "мне", "мой", "для", "по",
        "от", "из", "со", "у", "же", "ли", "это", "все", "покажи", "скажи", "найди", "найти", "поиск", "про", "есть",
        "можно", "сколько", "к", "ко", "об",
    )
}

# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/data/AppDatabase.kt
################################################################################
package com.example.retrodatabases.data

import android.content.Context
import androidx.room.Database
import androidx.room.Room
import androidx.room.RoomDatabase
import androidx.room.TypeConverters
import androidx.room.migration.Migration
import androidx.sqlite.db.SupportSQLiteDatabase
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed.DATABASE_VERSION
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed.seedDatabases
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed.seedRecords

@Database(
    entities = [DatabaseEntity::class, RecordEntity::class],
    version = DATABASE_VERSION,
    exportSchema = false,
)
@TypeConverters(Converters::class)
abstract class AppDatabase : RoomDatabase() {

    abstract fun libraryDao(): LibraryDao

    companion object {
        private const val FILE_NAME = "retro_databases.db"

        @Volatile
        private var instance: AppDatabase? = null

        fun get(context: Context): AppDatabase =
            instance ?: synchronized(this) {
                instance ?: buildDatabase(context.applicationContext).also { instance = it }
            }

        private fun buildDatabase(appContext: Context): AppDatabase =
            Room.databaseBuilder(appContext, AppDatabase::class.java, FILE_NAME)
                .addCallback(SeedCallback())
                .addMigrations(*seedMigrations.toTypedArray())
                .build()
    }
}

/**
 * Version [version] added database [version]. Copies one version lower get it from this migration; older copies run
 * it after the earlier migrations. Migrating never changes existing rows, so favourites and the records of the
 * earlier databases stay as they are.
 */
internal fun seedMigration(version: Int): Migration = object : Migration(version - 1, version) {
    override fun migrate(db: SupportSQLiteDatabase) {
        val added = setOf(version.toLong())
        seedDatabases.filter { it.id in added }.forEach { insertDatabase(db, it) }
        seedRecords.filter { it.databaseId in added }.forEach { insertRecord(db, it) }
    }
}

/** One migration for every version from 2 to [DATABASE_VERSION], in order. */
internal val seedMigrations: List<Migration> = (2..DATABASE_VERSION).map(::seedMigration)

/**
 * Fills the databases when the database file is first created.
 * Inserts run as SQL queries directly in onCreate, so there is no need to wait until the Room instance is ready.
 */
private class SeedCallback : RoomDatabase.Callback() {

    override fun onCreate(db: SupportSQLiteDatabase) {
        super.onCreate(db)

        seedDatabases.forEach { insertDatabase(db, it) }
        seedRecords.forEach { insertRecord(db, it) }
    }
}

private fun insertDatabase(db: SupportSQLiteDatabase, database: DatabaseEntity) {
    db.execSQL(
        "INSERT INTO databases (id, name, description, colorHex) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
        arrayOf<Any?>(database.id, database.name, database.description, database.colorHex),
    )
}

private fun insertRecord(db: SupportSQLiteDatabase, record: RecordEntity) {
    db.execSQL(
        """
        INSERT INTO records (databaseId, kind, section, title, originalTitle, author, year,
                             summary, details, instructions, example, rare, favorite)
        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0)
        """.trimIndent(),
        arrayOf<Any?>(
            record.databaseId,
            record.kind.name,
            record.section,
            record.title,
            record.originalTitle,
            record.author,
            record.year.toLong(),
            record.summary,
            record.details,
            record.instructions,
            record.example,
            if (record.rare) 1L else 0L,
        ),
    )
}

# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/data/Entities.kt

package com.example.retrodatabases.data

import androidx.room.Entity
import androidx.room.ForeignKey
import androidx.room.Index
import androidx.room.PrimaryKey

/** One database inside the app, for example "Database 1". */
@Entity(tableName = "databases")
data class DatabaseEntity(
    @PrimaryKey val id: Long,
    val name: String,
    val description: String,
    /** Accent colour of the database in #RRGGBB format. */
    val colorHex: String,
)

/** Catalogue record: a language, system, device, tool, practice, guide, project and so on. */
@Entity(
    tableName = "records",
    foreignKeys = [
        ForeignKey(
            entity = DatabaseEntity::class,
            parentColumns = ["id"],
            childColumns = ["databaseId"],
            onDelete = ForeignKey.CASCADE,
        ),
    ],
    indices = [Index("databaseId")],
)
data class RecordEntity(
    @PrimaryKey(autoGenerate = true) val id: Long = 0,
    val databaseId: Long,
    /** Kind of record: the top-level section of the catalogue. */
    val kind: Kind,
    /** Subsection inside the kind, for example "Imperative and system" or "Processors". */
    val section: String,
    val title: String,
    val originalTitle: String,
    val author: String,
    val year: Int,
    val summary: String,
    /** Details: for projects and guides, how everything is built and works. */
    val details: String,
    /** Step-by-step instructions: how to run it and how to use it. Null if not needed. */
    val instructions: String?,
    /** Code fragment (or several files with "### name" headings), or null. */
    val example: String?,
    /** Rare or little-known record; has its own filter. */
    val rare: Boolean = false,
    val favorite: Boolean = false,
)

/** One row of the database list screen: the database itself and its number of records. */
data class DatabaseSummary(
    val id: Long,
    val name: String,
    val description: String,
    val colorHex: String,
    val recordCount: Int,
)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data

/**

enum class Kind(val label: String) {
    LANGUAGE("Languages"),
    SYSTEM("Systems"),
    DEVICE("Devices"),
    TOOL("Tools"),
    PRACTICE("Practices"),
    GUIDE("Guides"),
    EXAMPLE("Examples"),

    CROSS("Cross-code"),
    MODEL("Economic models"),

# FILE: RetroDatabases/app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/data/LibraryDao.kt

package com.example.retrodatabases.data

import androidx.room.Dao
import androidx.room.Query
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow

@Dao
interface LibraryDao {

    @Query(
        """
        SELECT d.id AS id,
               d.name AS name,
               d.description AS description,
               d.colorHex AS colorHex,
               (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM records r WHERE r.databaseId = d.id) AS recordCount
        FROM databases d
        ORDER BY d.id
        """
    )
    fun observeDatabases(): Flow<List<DatabaseSummary>>

    @Query("SELECT * FROM databases WHERE id = :databaseId")
    fun observeDatabase(databaseId: Long): Flow<DatabaseEntity?>

    @Query("SELECT * FROM records WHERE databaseId = :databaseId ORDER BY year, title")
    fun observeRecords(databaseId: Long): Flow<List<RecordEntity>>

    @Query("SELECT * FROM records WHERE id = :recordId")
    fun observeRecord(recordId: Long): Flow<RecordEntity?>

    @Query("UPDATE records SET favorite = NOT favorite WHERE id = :recordId")
    suspend fun toggleFavorite(recordId: Long)

    /** Every database, for the assistant's index. Read once; the screens use the observe queries above. */
    @Query("SELECT * FROM databases ORDER BY id")
    suspend fun allDatabases(): List<DatabaseEntity>

    /** Every record, for the assistant's index. Read once; the screens use the observe queries above. */
    @Query("SELECT * FROM records")
    suspend fun allRecords(): List<RecordEntity>
}

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Cross-code experiment of 1046: the weekday of 25 December for 1040 to 1050 in the Julian reckoning, in Python and C. */
val db100Cross: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 100,
        kind = Kind.CROSS,
        section = "Calendars",
        title = "The weekdays of Christmas Day from 1040 to 1050, computed in Python and C",
        originalTitle = "The weekdays of Christmas Day from 1040 to 1050, computed in Python and C",
        author = "Julian calendar reckoners",
        year = 1046,
        summary = "Python and C programs find the weekday of 25 December for each year from 1040 to 1050 by the Julian leap rule, and a script shows that both print the same days.",
        details = "Christmas fell on a Thursday in 1040 and in 1046, and on a Sunday in 1043 and 1048, while the Julian leap rule makes every fourth year a leap year. The two programs use only whole-number arithmetic, so the result is exact, and it says nothing about the events of those Christmases.",
        rare = true,
        instructions = """
            1. Save the files below in one folder.
            2. Run the script: sh run.sh
        """,
        example = """
            ### weekdays.py
            NAMES = ["Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday"]

            def jan1_weekday(year):
                # Julian calendar: 1 January of year 1 was a Saturday; each earlier year adds 365 days and each fourth year a leap day
                days = (year - 1) * 365 + (year - 1) // 4
                return (6 + days) % 7

            for year in range(1040, 1051):
                # 25 December is day 358 of a common year and day 359 of a leap year, counted from 1 January
                offset = 359 if year % 4 == 0 else 358
                print(year, NAMES[(jan1_weekday(year) + offset) % 7])
            ### weekdays.c
            #include <stdio.h>

            static const char *names[] = {"Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday"};

            static int jan1_weekday(int year) {
                long days = (long)(year - 1) * 365 + (year - 1) / 4;
                return (int)((6 + days) % 7);
            }

            int main(void) {
                for (int year = 1040; year <= 1050; year++) {
                    int offset = (year % 4 == 0) ? 359 : 358;   /* 25 December, counted from 1 January */
                    printf("%d %s\n", year, names[(jan1_weekday(year) + offset) % 7]);
                }
                return 0;
            }
            ### run.sh
            python3 weekdays.py > python.txt
            cc -o weekdays_c weekdays.c
            ./weekdays_c > c.txt
            cat python.txt
            diff python.txt c.txt && echo "same result"
        """,
    ),

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Examples of 1046: the enthronement of Clement II on 25 December 1046, dated in the Julian and Gregorian reckonings. */
val db100Examples: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 100,
        kind = Kind.EXAMPLE,
        section = "Calendars",
        title = "The enthronement of Clement II on 25 December 1046, dated in two calendars",
        originalTitle = "The enthronement of Clement II on 25 December 1046, dated in two calendars",
        author = "Clement II and the Roman church",
        year = 1046,
        summary = "A short program gives the weekday of Clement II's enthronement, 25 December 1046 in the Julian reckoning, and converts the date into the Gregorian count, which is 31 December 1046.",
        details = "The Julian calendar was in use in the West in 1046, and the Gregorian count runs six days ahead of it that year, so one day carries two dates. The program finds the weekday by the Julian leap rule and by Python's Gregorian calendar, and both give a Thursday.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as clement_calendars.py.
            2. Run it: python3 clement_calendars.py
        """,
        example = """
            from datetime import date

            NAMES = ["Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday"]

            def julian_weekday(year, month, day):
                # 1 January of year 1 (Julian) was a Saturday; leap years are the years divisible by 4
                days_before_year = (year - 1) * 365 + (year - 1) // 4
                month_lengths = [31, 29 if year % 4 == 0 else 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31]
                days = days_before_year + sum(month_lengths[:month - 1]) + (day - 1)
                return NAMES[(6 + days) % 7]

            year, month, day = 1046, 12, 25
            offset = year // 100 - year // 400 - 2   # days the Gregorian count runs ahead of the Julian one
            gregorian = date(year, month, day + offset)
            print("Julian", day, "December", year, "is a", julian_weekday(year, month, day))
            print("the same day in the Gregorian count is", gregorian.day, "December", gregorian.year)
            print("Gregorian weekday check:", NAMES[(gregorian.weekday() + 1) % 7])
            print("days ahead in", year, "is", offset)
        """,
    ),

)

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Guides of 1041: how a page of baked clay type is set in an iron frame, printed and released for the next page. */
val db100Guides: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 100,
        kind = Kind.GUIDE,
        section = "Printing",
        title = "How a page of clay type is set in a frame, printed and released for the next page",
        originalTitle = "Huozi yinshua fa",
        author = "Bi Sheng, as described by Shen Kuo",
        year = 1041,
        summary = "The method sets baked clay types in an iron frame on a resin and wax plate, prints the page, then warms the frame so the types can be lifted out and used again.",
        details = "The method runs in these steps: carve each character on clay, harden the pieces by firing, set them in the frame over the plate, smooth the surface and print. The program keeps a stock of types, sets two pages from it and returns the types after each page, so the same stock serves both pages.",
        rare = true,
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as clay_type.py.
            2. Run it: python3 clay_type.py
        """,
        example = """
            # a stock of baked clay types, by character
            stock = {"A": 3, "B": 1, "C": 1}

            for page in ["ABACA", "CAB"]:
                frame = []
                for ch in page:
                    if stock[ch] == 0:
                        raise SystemExit("no type left for " + ch)
                    stock[ch] -= 1
                    frame.append(ch)
                print("page", "".join(frame), "printed, types still on hand:", sum(stock.values()))
                # the frame is warmed and the types are lifted out for the next page
                for ch in frame:
                    stock[ch] += 1
            print("types on hand after release:", sum(stock.values()))
        """,
    ),

)

    entry(
        databaseId = 100,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Dating",
        title = "The Song reign periods Kangding and Qingli, with their calendar years counted",
        originalTitle = "The Song reign periods Kangding and Qingli, with their calendar years counted",
        author = "Song imperial chancery",
        year = 1041,
        summary = "A short program counts the calendar years of the Song reign periods Kangding and Qingli, which together cover the years 1040 to 1048, and adds them up.",
        details = "Kangding is dated to 1040 and 1041 and Qingli to 1041 to 1048, so the two periods share the year 1041. The next period, Huangyou, is left out because accounts differ on when it ended, giving 1053 in one list and 1054 in another.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as song_periods.py.
            2. Run it: python3 song_periods.py
        """,
        example = """
            # reign periods of the Song with their first and last calendar years, as commonly given
            periods = [("Kangding", 1040, 1041), ("Qingli", 1041, 1048)]
            total = 0
            longest = None
            shortest = None
            for name, first, last in periods:
                years = last - first + 1
                total += years
                print(name, first, last, years)
                if longest is None or years > longest[1]:
                    longest = (name, years)
                if shortest is None or years < shortest[1]:
                    shortest = (name, years)
            print("periods:", len(periods))
            print("total years:", total)
            print("longest:", longest[0], longest[1], "years")
            print("shortest:", shortest[0], shortest[1], "years")
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Cross-code experiment of 1037: the days from the battle of Stiklestad to Conrad II's Constitutio, counted in Python and in C. */
val db101Cross: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 101,
        kind = Kind.CROSS,
        section = "Dates",
        title = "Days from the battle of Stiklestad to Conrad II's Constitutio in Python and C",
        originalTitle = "Days between two fixed dates",
        author = "Olaf II of Norway and Conrad II",
        year = 1037,
        summary = "Python and C programs count the days from the battle of Stiklestad on 29 July 1030 to Conrad II's Constitutio on 28 May 1037, and a script checks that both give 2495.",
        details = "The C program counts days with a Julian leap rule and no date library, while the Python program uses date objects, and both count the leap days of 1032 and 1036 alike. The dates are given as commonly stated, so the run tests the arithmetic rather than the events.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the files below in one folder.
            2. Run the script: sh run.sh
        """,
        example = """
            ### stiklestad.py
            from datetime import date

            stiklestad = date(1030, 7, 29)    # the battle of Stiklestad, as commonly given
            constitutio = date(1037, 5, 28)   # Conrad II's Constitutio de feudis, as commonly given
            print("days from Stiklestad to the Constitutio:", (constitutio - stiklestad).days)
            ### stiklestad.c
            #include <stdio.h>

            static int is_leap(int y) { return y % 4 == 0; }   /* Julian rule: no century exceptions */

            static long day_number(int y, int m, int d) {
                static const int days_before[] = {0, 31, 59, 90, 120, 151, 181, 212, 243, 273, 304, 334};
                long n = 0;
                for (int year = 1; year < y; year++) n += is_leap(year) ? 366 : 365;
                n += days_before[m - 1];
                if (m > 2 && is_leap(y)) n += 1;
                return n + d;
            }

            int main(void) {
                long start = day_number(1030, 7, 29);   /* Stiklestad, as commonly given */
                long end = day_number(1037, 5, 28);     /* Constitutio, as commonly given */
                printf("days from Stiklestad to the Constitutio: %ld\n", end - start);
                return 0;
            }
            ### run.sh
            python3 stiklestad.py > python.txt
            cc -o stiklestad_c stiklestad.c
            ./stiklestad_c > c.txt
            cat python.txt
            diff python.txt c.txt && echo "same result"
        """,
    ),

)

        author = "Maya scribes who carved Long Count dates",
        year = 1030,
        summary = "A short program turns the Long Count date 9.12.11.16.4 into a count of days from its base date, converts the count back, and prints a check.",
        details = "The Long Count is older than this record: it was devised in the Preclassic period, and Maya inscriptions counted days from a fixed base with it for centuries before 1030. The year 1030 is a placement, not the date of any inscription, and in the Postclassic kingdoms of Yucatan the Short Count had replaced it.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as long_count.py.
            2. Run it: python3 long_count.py
        """,
        example = """
            PLACES = [144000, 7200, 360, 20, 1]    # days in a baktun, katun, tun, winal and kin
            long_count = [9, 12, 11, 16, 4]        # the date 9.12.11.16.4

            days = sum(digit * place for digit, place in zip(long_count, PLACES))
            print("days since 0.0.0.0.0:", days)

            back = []
            rest = days
            for place in PLACES:
                back.append(rest // place)
                rest = rest % place
            print("written back:", ".".join(str(digit) for digit in back))
            print("check:", "ok" if back == long_count else "wrong")
        """,
        rare = true,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Projects of 1031 to 1039: the day of the year on which five rulers of the decade died, counted by a short program. */
val db101Projects: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 101,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Calendar",
        title = "The day of the year on which five rulers of the 1030s died",
        originalTitle = "The day of the year on which five rulers of the 1030s died",
        author = "Robert II, Rudolf III, Romanos III, Stephen I and Conrad II",
        year = 1039,
        summary = "A short program counts the day of the year for five rulers' deaths between 1031 and 1039 and prints the days left in each year.",
        details = "Each date is the one usually given for the death of the ruler named. Accounts differ on the day of Romanos III's death: 11 April 1034 is the usual date, while the chronicle of John Skylitzes gives 15 April, and the program uses 11 April. The count starts at 1 January as day 1, and 1032 is the only leap year among the five dates, so its extra day is counted.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as rulers_day_of_year.py.
            2. Run it: python3 rulers_day_of_year.py
        """,
        example = """
            DAYS_BEFORE = [0, 31, 59, 90, 120, 151, 181, 212, 243, 273, 304, 334]


            def is_leap(year):
                return year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0)


            def day_of_year(year, month, day):
                extra = 1 if month > 2 and is_leap(year) else 0
                return DAYS_BEFORE[month - 1] + extra + day


            deaths = [
                ("Robert II of France", 1031, 7, 20),
                ("Rudolf III of Burgundy", 1032, 9, 6),
                ("Romanos III", 1034, 4, 11),
                ("Stephen I of Hungary", 1038, 8, 15),
                ("Conrad II", 1039, 6, 4),
            ]

            leap_count = 0
            for name, year, month, day in deaths:
                length = 366 if is_leap(year) else 365
                n = day_of_year(year, month, day)
                leap_count += 1 if is_leap(year) else 0
                print(f"{name} ({year}): day {n} of the year, {length - n} days left")
            print("leap years among the items:", leap_count)
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Cross-code experiment of 1026: the positions of three notes in Guido's gamut, found by a Python program and a C program. */
val db102Cross: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 102,
        kind = Kind.CROSS,
        section = "Music",
        title = "The positions of three notes in Guido's gamut, in Python and C",
        originalTitle = "The positions of three notes in Guido's gamut, in Python and C",
        author = "Guido of Arezzo",
        year = 1026,
        summary = "Two programs look up three note names in Guido's gamut of twenty notes and print the same positions in Python and in C.",
        details = "The gamut runs from the lowest gamma to the double e, twenty notes in all, and it is usually linked with Guido's teaching. The date is approximate, since the exact origin of the gamut is uncertain, and the run script checks that the two programs print the same lines.",
        rare = true,
        instructions = """
            1. Save the files below in one folder.
            2. Run the script: sh run.sh
        """,
        example = """
            ### gamut.py
            gamut = ["Gamma", "A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f", "g", "aa", "bb", "cc", "dd", "ee"]
            for note in ["Gamma", "e", "ee"]:
                print(note, "is at position", gamut.index(note))
            print("notes in the gamut:", len(gamut))
            ### gamut.c
            #include <stdio.h>
            #include <string.h>

            int main(void) {
                const char *gamut[] = {"Gamma", "A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f", "g", "aa", "bb", "cc", "dd", "ee"};
                const char *wanted[] = {"Gamma", "e", "ee"};
                int count = sizeof gamut / sizeof gamut[0];
                for (int w = 0; w < 3; w++) {
                    for (int p = 0; p < count; p++) {
                        if (strcmp(gamut[p], wanted[w]) == 0) {
                            printf("%s is at position %d\n", wanted[w], p);
                        }
                    }
                }
                printf("notes in the gamut: %d\n", count);
                return 0;
            }
            ### run.sh
            python3 gamut.py > python.txt
            cc -o gamut_c gamut.c
            ./gamut_c > c.txt
            cat python.txt
            diff python.txt c.txt && echo "same result"
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Guides of 1020 to 1030: how a hill's height and the dip of the horizon give the Earth's radius, as Biruni reckoned it. */
val db102Guides: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 102,
        kind = Kind.GUIDE,
        section = "Geodesy",
        title = "How a hill's height and the dip of the horizon give the Earth's radius",
        originalTitle = "How a hill's height and the dip of the horizon give the Earth's radius",
        author = "Abu Rayhan al-Biruni",
        year = 1025,
        summary = "Biruni's method takes the height of a hill and the dip of the horizon seen from its top, and gives the Earth's radius, which he worked out near Nandana in the early eleventh century.",
        details = "The hill is given as 652 cubits high and the dip as 34 arcminutes, and the formula R = h cos d / (1 - cos d) gives the radius in cubits, which some accounts convert to about 6,340 km. The sources date the measurement only to the early eleventh century, so the year here is approximate.",
        rare = true,
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as biruni_radius.py.
            2. Run it: python3 biruni_radius.py
        """,
        example = """
            import math

            height = 652                         # the hill's height in cubits, as commonly given
            dip = math.radians(34 / 60)          # the dip of the horizon, 34 arcminutes
            c = math.cos(dip)
            radius = height * c / (1 - c)        # from cos(dip) = R / (R + height)
            print("radius of the Earth in thousands of cubits:", round(radius / 1000))
        """,
    ),

)

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Projects of 1020 to 1030: a short program that sorts three dated deaths of 1024 and 1025 and counts the days between them. */
val db102Projects: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 102,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Rulers",
        title = "Days between three deaths of 1024 and 1025, in date order",
        originalTitle = "Days between three deaths of 1024 and 1025, in date order",
        author = "Benedict VIII, Henry II and Basil II",
        year = 1024,
        summary = "Benedict VIII, Henry II and Basil II died on 9 April 1024, 13 July 1024 and 15 December 1025, and a short program sorts the three dates and counts the days between them.",
        details = "The dates are given as commonly stated, and Python's calendar does the counting, so the program checks date arithmetic and not the reigns of the three men. The result is 95 days from the first death to the second, 520 from the second to the third, and 615 in all.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as rulers_deaths.py.
            2. Run it: python3 rulers_deaths.py
        """,
        example = """
            from datetime import date

            deaths = [
                ("Henry II", date(1024, 7, 13)),
                ("Benedict VIII", date(1024, 4, 9)),
                ("Basil II", date(1025, 12, 15)),
            ]
            deaths.sort(key=lambda item: item[1])
            for (name_a, day_a), (name_b, day_b) in zip(deaths, deaths[1:]):
                print("days from", name_a, "to", name_b + ":", (day_b - day_a).days)
            print("first to last:", (deaths[-1][1] - deaths[0][1]).days)
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Cross-code experiment of 1016: the days from Aethelred II's death to Cnut's death, counted in Python and in C. */
val db103Cross: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 103,
        kind = Kind.CROSS,
        section = "Dates",
        title = "Days from Aethelred II's death to Cnut's death in Python and C",
        originalTitle = "Days between two fixed dates",
        author = "Aethelred II and Cnut the Great",
        year = 1016,
        summary = "Python and C programs count the days from Aethelred II's death on 23 April 1016 to Cnut's death on 12 November 1035, and both give the same count of 7142.",
        details = "The C program counts days with its own leap-year rule and no date library, while the Python program uses the calendar, and both give the same count. The span holds no century year, so the Julian and Gregorian reckonings give the same number of days, and the run tests the arithmetic rather than the reigns.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the first program as aethelred_cnut.py and the second as aethelred_cnut.c.
            2. Run the Python program with python3 aethelred_cnut.py, then compile and run the C program with cc -o aethelred_cnut_c aethelred_cnut.c and ./aethelred_cnut_c.
        """,
        example = """
            ### aethelred_cnut.py
            from datetime import date

            aethelred = date(1016, 4, 23)     # Aethelred II's death, as commonly given
            cnut = date(1035, 11, 12)         # Cnut's death, as commonly given
            print("days from Aethelred II's death to Cnut's death:", (cnut - aethelred).days)
            ### aethelred_cnut.c
            #include <stdio.h>

            static int is_leap(int y) { return (y % 4 == 0 && y % 100 != 0) || y % 400 == 0; }

            static long day_number(int y, int m, int d) {
                static const int days_before[] = {0, 31, 59, 90, 120, 151, 181, 212, 243, 273, 304, 334};
                long n = 0;
                for (int year = 1; year < y; year++) n += is_leap(year) ? 366 : 365;
                n += days_before[m - 1];
                if (m > 2 && is_leap(y)) n += 1;
                return n + d;
            }

            int main(void) {
                long start = day_number(1016, 4, 23);   /* Aethelred II's death, as commonly given */
                long end = day_number(1035, 11, 12);    /* Cnut's death, as commonly given */
                printf("days from Aethelred II's death to Cnut's death: %ld\n", end - start);
                return 0;
            }
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Guides of 1010: al-Karaji's argument that the cubes of the first whole numbers add up to a square, written out as a short program. */
val db103Guides: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 103,
        kind = Kind.GUIDE,
        section = "Algebra",
        title = "How al-Karaji's argument shows the cubes of 1 to n add up to a square",
        originalTitle = "How al-Karaji's argument shows the cubes of 1 to n add up to a square",
        author = "Abu Bakr al-Karaji",
        year = 1010,
        summary = "Al-Karaji's argument, as later writers give it, shows that the cubes of the first n whole numbers add up to the square of their running sum, and a short program checks the steps for n up to 6 and at n = 10.",
        details = "At each step the running sum grows by n, and the square of the running sum grows by exactly n cubed, so the two totals match for every n. The case n = 10 gives 3025, which is 55 squared, and whether this is induction in al-Karaji's own sense is a matter of interpretation.",
        rare = true,
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as cubes.py.
            2. Run it: python3 cubes.py
        """,
        example = """
            total_cubes = 0
            running_sum = 0
            for n in range(1, 7):
                total_cubes += n ** 3
                running_sum += n
                print(n, total_cubes, running_sum * running_sum)
            print("n = 10:", sum(k ** 3 for k in range(1, 11)), (10 * 11 // 2) ** 2)
            print("cubes equal squares at n = 6:", total_cubes == running_sum * running_sum)
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Projects of 1016: the reigns of three emperors of Japan from 986 to 1036, listed and totalled in code. */
val db103Projects: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 103,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Japan",
        title = "Reign lengths of Ichijo, Sanjo and Go-Ichijo, emperors of Japan from 986 to 1036",
        originalTitle = "Ichijo, Sanjo and Go-Ichijo",
        author = "The Heian court",
        year = 1016,
        summary = "A short program lists the reigns of three Heian emperors, totals their years and picks out the longest and the shortest reign.",
        details = "The reign dates used are the usual ones: Ichijo 986 to 1011, Sanjo 1011 to 1016 and Go-Ichijo 1016 to 1036, giving reigns of 25, 5 and 20 years. The example tests the arithmetic of the dates and says nothing about the politics of the period.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as emperors.py.
            2. Run it: python3 emperors.py
        """,
        example = """
            REIGNS = [
                ("Ichijo", 986, 1011),
                ("Sanjo", 1011, 1016),
                ("Go-Ichijo", 1016, 1036),
            ]
            lengths = []
            for name, start, end in REIGNS:
                years = end - start
                lengths.append((years, name))
                print(name, years, "years")
            print("emperors:", len(REIGNS))
            print("total years:", sum(years for years, _ in lengths))
            print("longest:", max(lengths)[1], max(lengths)[0], "years")
            print("shortest:", min(lengths)[1], min(lengths)[0], "years")
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Cross-code experiment of 1002: the days from the death of Otto III to St Brice's Day, counted in Python and in C. */
val db104Cross: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 104,
        kind = Kind.CROSS,
        section = "Dates",
        title = "Days from the death of Otto III to St Brice's Day in Python and C",
        originalTitle = "Days from the death of Otto III to St Brice's Day in Python and C",
        author = "Otto III and Aethelred II",
        year = 1002,
        summary = "Python and C programs count the days from the death of Otto III on 24 January 1002 to St Brice's Day on 13 November 1002, and a script checks that both give 293.",
        details = "The C program counts days with its own leap-year rule and no date library, while the Python program uses the calendar, and both count the days of the non-leap year 1002 alike. The dates are given as commonly stated, so the run tests the arithmetic rather than the events.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the files below in one folder.
            2. Run the script: sh run.sh
        """,
        example = """
            ### otto_brice.py
            from datetime import date

            otto_death = date(1002, 1, 24)     # death of Otto III, as commonly stated
            brice = date(1002, 11, 13)         # St Brice's Day massacre, as commonly stated
            print("days from Otto III's death to St Brice's Day:", (brice - otto_death).days)
            ### otto_brice.c
            #include <stdio.h>

            static int is_leap(int y) { return (y % 4 == 0 && y % 100 != 0) || y % 400 == 0; }

            static long day_number(int y, int m, int d) {
                static const int days_before[] = {0, 31, 59, 90, 120, 151, 181, 212, 243, 273, 304, 334};
                long n = 0;
                for (int year = 1; year < y; year++) n += is_leap(year) ? 366 : 365;
                n += days_before[m - 1];
                if (m > 2 && is_leap(y)) n += 1;
                return n + d;
            }

            int main(void) {
                long start = day_number(1002, 1, 24);   /* death of Otto III, as commonly stated */
                long end = day_number(1002, 11, 13);    /* St Brice's Day massacre, as commonly stated */
                printf("days from Otto III's death to St Brice's Day: %ld\n", end - start);
                return 0;
            }
            ### run.sh
            python3 otto_brice.py > python.txt
            cc -o otto_brice_c otto_brice.c
            ./otto_brice_c > c.txt
            cat python.txt
            diff python.txt c.txt && echo "same result"
        """,
    ),

)

/** Examples of 1000: the leap years of 1000 to 1010 counted under the Julian rule and under the Gregorian rule. */
val db104Examples: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 104,
        kind = Kind.EXAMPLE,
        section = "Calendar",
        title = "Leap years of 1000 to 1010 under the Julian rule and under the Gregorian rule",
        originalTitle = "Leap years of 1000 to 1010 under the Julian rule and under the Gregorian rule",
        author = "Julius Caesar and Pope Gregory XIII",
        year = 1000,
        summary = "Year 1000 is a leap year under the Julian rule used in Europe but not under the Gregorian rule, so the two rules count 3 and 2 leap years from 1000 to 1010.",
        details = "The Julian rule makes every fourth year a leap year, while the Gregorian rule of 1582 leaves out century years that are not divisible by 400. The Gregorian rule is applied to 1000 only for comparison, since the Gregorian calendar was not adopted until 1582.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as leap_rules.py.
            2. Run it: python3 leap_rules.py
        """,
        example = """
            def julian_leap(year):
                return year % 4 == 0


            def gregorian_leap(year):
                return year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0)


            years = range(1000, 1011)
            julian = [y for y in years if julian_leap(y)]
            gregorian = [y for y in years if gregorian_leap(y)]
            print("Julian leap years:", julian)
            print("Gregorian leap years:", gregorian)
            print("counts, Julian and Gregorian:", len(julian), len(gregorian))
            print("1000 is a leap year, Julian:", julian_leap(1000), "Gregorian:", gregorian_leap(1000))
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** A guide of 1000: how a product of two cosines becomes half a sum of cosines, the rule behind Ibn Yunus's timing procedures. */
val db104Guides: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 104,
        kind = Kind.GUIDE,
        section = "Trigonometry",
        title = "How a product of two cosines becomes half a sum of cosines",
        originalTitle = "Zij al-Kabir al-Hakimi",
        author = "Ibn Yunus, with the identity named after Johannes Werner",
        year = 1000,
        summary = "A product of two cosines equals half the sum of the cosine of the difference of the angles and the cosine of their sum, a rule that turns a multiplication into two table look-ups, an addition and a halving.",
        details = "Johannes Werner wrote the identity down in a sixteenth-century text on conic sections, and in 1819 Delambre found that two of Ibn Yunus's altitude-based timing procedures amount to the same rule. Prosthaphaeresis used this kind of identity to multiply numbers with sine and cosine tables, and the program below checks the rule for exact cosines of 0, 60, 120 and 180 degrees.",
        rare = true,
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as cosine_product.py.
            2. Run it: python3 cosine_product.py
        """,
        example = """
            from fractions import Fraction

            # exact cosines at 0, 60, 120 and 180 degrees
            table = {0: Fraction(1), 60: Fraction(1, 2), 120: Fraction(-1, 2), 180: Fraction(-1)}


            def cos_deg(angle):
                angle = angle % 360
                if angle > 180:
                    angle = 360 - angle
                return table[angle]


            def by_sum_rule(a, b):
                # cos a * cos b = (cos(a - b) + cos(a + b)) / 2
                return (cos_deg(a - b) + cos_deg(a + b)) / 2


            pairs = [(0, 60), (60, 60), (60, 120), (120, 180), (180, 180)]
            agree = True
            for a, b in pairs:
                direct = cos_deg(a) * cos_deg(b)
                summed = by_sum_rule(a, b)
                agree = agree and direct == summed
                print(f"cos {a} * cos {b} = {direct}, by the sum rule {summed}")
            print("all pairs agree:", agree)
        """,
    ),

)

val db104Projects: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 104,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Dates",
        title = "Dated events of 1002 to 1010, sorted and spaced by years",
        originalTitle = "Dated events of 1002 to 1010, sorted and spaced by years",
        author = "Various rulers and observers",
        year = 1002,
        summary = "Five dated events of 1002 to 1010, from Spain, China, Egypt, India and the sky, are sorted by a short program that reports the years between them.",
        details = "The events are the death of Almanzor at Medinaceli in 1002, the treaty of Shanyuan in 1005, the supernova SN 1006, the destruction of the Holy Sepulchre church ordered by al-Hakim in 1009, and the consecration of the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur in 1010. The program sorts them, lists the gaps between neighbours and averages them, and the years are given as commonly stated, so the run tests the arithmetic rather than the events.",
        rare = true,
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as dated_events.py.
            2. Run it: python3 dated_events.py
        """,
        example = """
            # Five dated events of 1002 to 1010, listed out of order at first
            events = [
                (1009, "Holy Sepulchre church destroyed"),
                (1002, "death of Almanzor at Medinaceli"),
                (1010, "Brihadeeswara temple consecrated"),
                (1006, "supernova SN 1006 seen"),
                (1005, "treaty of Shanyuan"),
            ]

            events.sort()
            gaps = [later[0] - earlier[0] for earlier, later in zip(events, events[1:])]
            print("events:", len(events))
            print("first:", events[0][0], events[0][1])
            print("last:", events[-1][0], events[-1][1])
            print("span in years:", events[-1][0] - events[0][0])
            print("gaps:", gaps)
            print("largest gap:", max(gaps))
            print("smallest gap:", min(gaps))
            print("average gap:", sum(gaps) / len(gaps))
            print("gaps of one year:", sum(1 for gap in gaps if gap == 1))
        """,
    ),

)

        author = "Abu Mahmud al-Khujandi",

        summary = "A Python program and a C program turn the latitude of Rayy read by al-Khujandi in 994 into 35.5773 decimal degrees, and a script tests that both agree.",
        details = "The latitude comes from the same 994 readings as the tilt, and both programs convert the same minutes and seconds with the same formula, so the run tests the arithmetic rather than the readings. Each program prints four decimals, and the script compares the two outputs.",
        rare = true,
        instructions = """
            1. Save the files below in one folder.
            2. Run the script: sh run.sh
        """,
        example = """
            ### latitude.py
            deg, minutes, seconds = 35, 34, 38.45
            latitude = deg + minutes / 60 + seconds / 3600
            print(f"{latitude:.4f}")
            ### latitude.c
            #include <stdio.h>

            int main(void) {
                double deg = 35, minutes = 34, seconds = 38.45;
                double latitude = deg + minutes / 60 + seconds / 3600;
                printf("%.4f\n", latitude);
                return 0;
            }
            ### run.sh
            python3 latitude.py > python.txt
            cc -o latitude_c latitude.c
            ./latitude_c > c.txt
            cat python.txt
            diff python.txt c.txt && echo "same result"
        """,
    ),

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** A guide of 994: how the sun's noon heights at the two solstices give the tilt of the ecliptic. */
val db105Guides: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 105,
        kind = Kind.GUIDE,
        section = "Astronomy",
        title = "How the sun's noon heights at the two solstices give the tilt of the ecliptic",
        originalTitle = "How the sun's noon heights at the two solstices give the tilt of the ecliptic",
        author = "Abu Mahmud al-Khujandi",
        year = 994,
        summary = "Half the difference between the sun's noon heights at the two solstices gives the tilt of the ecliptic, the meridian method of the kind al-Khujandi used at Rayy.",
        details = "At the June solstice the noon height is 90 degrees minus the latitude plus the tilt, and at the December solstice it is 90 minus the latitude minus the tilt, so half the difference is the tilt and the latitude cancels out. The program uses the latitude of Rayy and the tilt of 23 degrees 32 minutes 19 seconds to work out the two heights, then reverses the method to recover the tilt.",
        rare = true,
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as tilt_from_heights.py.
            2. Run it: python3 tilt_from_heights.py
        """,
        example = """
            # Tilt of the ecliptic from the sun's noon heights at the two solstices.
            # The heights are worked out from the Rayy latitude and tilt, then the method is reversed.
            phi = 35 + 34 / 60 + 38.45 / 3600      # latitude of Rayy
            eps = 23 + 32 / 60 + 19 / 3600         # tilt of the ecliptic

            summer = 90 - phi + eps                # noon height at the June solstice
            winter = 90 - phi - eps                # noon height at the December solstice

            tilt = (summer - winter) / 2           # the method: half the difference
            print(f"summer noon height {summer:.4f} degrees")
            print(f"winter noon height {winter:.4f} degrees")
            print(f"tilt from the two heights {tilt:.4f} degrees")
            print("matches the tilt used:", abs(tilt - eps) < 1e-9)
        """,
    ),

)

    entry(
        databaseId = 105,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Rulers",
        title = "Reigns of five rulers who held power in the 990s, summed and ranked",
        originalTitle = "Reigns of five rulers who held power in the 990s, summed and ranked",
        author = "Basil II, Song Taizong, Song Zhenzong, Hugh Capet and Robert II",
        year = 997,
        summary = "Five reigns that overlap the 990s add up to 139 years, and ranked by length Basil II's 49 years come first and Hugh Capet's 9 years come last.",
        details = "The list is a compilation and has no date of its own, so 997 is a placed year: it is the year Song Zhenzong succeeded Song Taizong, one of the reigns in the list. The reign years are taken as commonly stated, and each length is the difference between the end year and the start year.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as reigns_90s.py.
            2. Run it: python3 reigns_90s.py
        """,
        example = """
            # Reigns of five rulers who held power in the 990s, in years as commonly stated.
            reigns = [
                ("Basil II", 976, 1025),
                ("Song Taizong", 976, 997),
                ("Song Zhenzong", 997, 1022),
                ("Hugh Capet", 987, 996),
                ("Robert II", 996, 1031),
            ]

            lengths = [(name, end - start) for name, start, end in reigns]
            ranked = sorted(lengths, key=lambda item: item[1], reverse=True)
            total = sum(years for _, years in lengths)

            print("rulers:", len(lengths))
            print("total years:", total)
            print(f"longest: {ranked[0][0]} {ranked[0][1]} years")
            print(f"shortest: {ranked[-1][0]} {ranked[-1][1]} years")
            print("ranked:")
            for name, years in ranked:
                print(f"{name} {years}")
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Cross-code experiment of 987: the ten sections of Ibn al-Nadim's Fihrist, counted in Python and in C. */
val db106Cross: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 106,
        kind = Kind.CROSS,
        section = "Baghdad",
        title = "The ten sections of the Fihrist, six Islamic and four other, counted in Python and C",
        originalTitle = "The ten sections of the Fihrist, six Islamic and four other, counted in Python and C",
        author = "Ibn al-Nadim",
        year = 987,
        summary = "Python and C programs count the ten sections of the Fihrist, six on Islamic writings and four on non-Islamic works, and a script checks that both print the same result.",
        details = "The C program uses an array and a loop, while the Python program uses a list of pairs, and both must print the six Islamic and four non-Islamic sections and a total of ten. The example tests a short fixed list of counts in two languages.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the files below in one folder.
            2. Run the script: sh run.sh
        """,
        example = """
            ### sections.py
            sections = [("Islamic writings", 6), ("non-Islamic works and translations", 4)]
            total = 0
            for name, count in sections:
                print(name, count)
                total += count
            print("sections in all:", total)
            ### sections.c
            #include <stdio.h>

            int main(void) {
                const char *names[] = {"Islamic writings", "non-Islamic works and translations"};
                int counts[] = {6, 4};
                int total = 0;
                for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
                    printf("%s %d\n", names[i], counts[i]);
                    total += counts[i];
                }
                printf("sections in all: %d\n", total);
                return 0;
            }
            ### run.sh
            python3 sections.py > python.txt
            cc -o sections_c sections.c
            ./sections_c > c.txt
            cat python.txt
            diff python.txt c.txt && echo "same result"
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Projects of 980 to 990: the accession years of five rulers, sorted and spaced by a short program. */
val db106Projects: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 106,
        kind = Kind.PROJECT,
        section = "Rulers",
        title = "The accession years of five rulers of the 980s, put in order with their gaps",
        originalTitle = "The accession years of five rulers of the 980s, put in order with their gaps",
        author = "Five rulers of the 980s",
        year = 987,
        summary = "A short program sorts the accession years of five rulers of the 980s and prints the gap between each pair of neighbours in the list.",
        details = "The rulers are Le Hoan, Otto III, the Japanese emperor Kazan, Rajaraja I and Hugh Capet, and each year is the year that ruler came to power. The gaps show how the accessions followed one another across the decade.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as rulers.py.
            2. Run it: python3 rulers.py
        """,
        example = """
            rulers = [
                ("Hugh Capet", 987),
                ("Le Hoan", 980),
                ("Rajaraja I", 985),
                ("Otto III", 983),
                ("Kazan", 984),
            ]
            rulers.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[1])
            previous = None
            for name, year in rulers:
                gap = "" if previous is None else f" (+{year - previous})"
                print(f"{year} {name}{gap}")
                previous = year
            print("rulers:", len(rulers))
            print("span:", rulers[-1][1] - rulers[0][1], "years")
        """,
    ),

)

package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed

import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind
import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity

/** Cross-code experiment of 971: the years of carving of the Shu canon, from 971 to 983 with both ends included, counted in Python and in C. */
val db107Cross: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(

    entry(
        databaseId = 107,
        kind = Kind.CROSS,
        section = "Dates",
        title = "The years of carving of the Shu canon, 971 to 983, counted in Python and C",
        originalTitle = "The years of carving of the Shu canon, 971 to 983, counted in Python and C",
        author = "Song court commission",
        year = 971,
        summary = "Python and C programs count the years from 971 to 983 with both ends included, and a script checks that both give 13.",
        details = "Most accounts put the start of the carving at 971 and the finish at 983, and one gives 972 as the start, which would make 12 years. The C program counts with its own loop and no date library, while the Python program uses plain arithmetic, so the run tests the counting rather than the events.",
        instructions = """
            1. Save the example as shu_span.py, shu_span.c and run.sh.
            2. Run it: sh run.sh
        """,
        example = """
            ### shu_span.py
            first = 971   # start of the carving, as most accounts give it
            last = 983    # finish of the carving
            print("years of carving, both ends included:", last - first + 1)
            ### shu_span.c
            #include <stdio.h>

            int main(void) {
                int first = 971;   /* start of the carving, as most accounts give it */
                int last = 983;    /* finish of the carving */
                int years = 0;
                for (int y = first; y <= last; y++) years++;
                printf("years of carving, both ends included: %d\n", years);
                return 0;
            }
            ### run.sh
            python3 shu_span.py > python.txt
            cc -o shu_span_c shu_span.c
            ./shu_span_c > c.txt
            cat python.txt
            diff python.txt c.txt && echo "same result"
        """,
    ),

)
