################################################################################
# FILE: RetroDatabases/tools/build_catalogue.py
################################################################################
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Builds the catalogue from tools/databases.json and the record files, then checks every record.

Usage:
  python3 tools/build_catalogue.py          rewrite the generated parts, then run the checks
  python3 tools/build_catalogue.py --check  run the checks only and write nothing

Rewrites, from the spec and the record files:
  app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/data/seed/SeedCatalog.kt  (the whole file)
  CATALOGUE.md        the sections between the GENERATED CATALOGUE markers (databases not curated by hand)
  README.md           the blocks between the GENERATED OVERVIEW and GENERATED STRUCTURE markers

Checks: database ids and colours, the record files of every database, and for quota databases
(the 50-record batches) the kind counts, the runnable records, the rare flags, the years and the
text rules. Titles repeated anywhere in the catalogue are reported too.
Exit status is 1 when a check fails, so the script can run before the Gradle build.
"""
import argparse
import collections
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SEED = ROOT / "app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/data/seed"
SPEC = ROOT / "tools/databases.json"
CATALOGUE = ROOT / "CATALOGUE.md"
README = ROOT / "README.md"
SEED_CATALOG = SEED / "SeedCatalog.kt"
ECONOMICS = ROOT / "tools/economics"
MODELS_SPEC = ECONOMICS / "models.json"
SPHERES_SPEC = ECONOMICS / "spheres.json"

KINDS = ["LANGUAGE", "SYSTEM", "DEVICE", "TOOL", "PRACTICE", "GUIDE", "EXAMPLE", "PROJECT", "FLEX", "CROSS"]
KIND_LABELS = {"LANGUAGE": "Languages", "SYSTEM": "Systems", "DEVICE": "Devices", "TOOL": "Tools",
               "PRACTICE": "Practices", "GUIDE": "Guides", "EXAMPLE": "Examples", "PROJECT": "Projects",
               "FLEX": "Flex", "CROSS": "Cross-code", "MODEL": "Economic models", "COMPROMISE": "Compromises"}
ECONOMY_KINDS = ["MODEL", "COMPROMISE"]
# Words allowed in summary and details, as low and high limits: (summary low, summary high, details low, details high)
ECONOMY_WORDS = {"MODEL": (12, 70, 25, 110), "COMPROMISE": (20, 90, 40, 170)}
ECONOMY_YEAR = 2026
ECONOMY_AUTHOR = "This catalogue, as a proposal (not an established model)"
COMPROMISE_ORIGINAL = "Compromise proposal"
QUOTA_COUNTS = {"LANGUAGE": 6, "SYSTEM": 5, "DEVICE": 8, "TOOL": 6, "PRACTICE": 5,
                "GUIDE": 5, "EXAMPLE": 6, "PROJECT": 4, "FLEX": 3, "CROSS": 2}
RUNNABLE = {"GUIDE", "EXAMPLE", "PROJECT", "FLEX", "CROSS"}
FILE_SUFFIXES = ["Languages", "Systems", "Devices", "Tools", "Practices", "Guides", "Examples",
                 "Projects", "Flex", "Cross", "Catalog"]
FORBIDDEN = ["(memory)", "memory, not checked", "search source", "single source", "not checked",
             "checked in this batch", "web search", "wikipedia"]
ALLOWED_DUPLICATE_TITLES = {"Erlang", "Software inspections"}  # already in databases 1 and 2

ENTRY = re.compile(r"^    entry\(\n(.*?)^    \),", re.S | re.M)
TITLE = re.compile(r'title = "([^"]*)"')
KIND = re.compile(r"kind = Kind\.(\w+)")
YEAR = re.compile(r"year = (\d{1,4})")
DATABASE_ID = re.compile(r"databaseId = (\d+)")
CYRILLIC = re.compile(r"[\u0400-\u04FF]")


def load_spec(problems):
    rows = json.loads(SPEC.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    ids = [row["id"] for row in rows]
    if ids != list(range(1, len(rows) + 1)):
        problems.append("spec: ids must run 1 to N in order")
    colours = [row["colorHex"] for row in rows]
    if len(set(colours)) != len(colours):
        problems.append("spec: a colour is used twice")
    names = [row["name"] for row in rows]
    if len(set(names)) != len(names):
        problems.append("spec: a database name is used twice")
    for row in rows:
        if not re.fullmatch(r"#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}", row["colorHex"]):
            problems.append(f"database {row['id']}: colour {row['colorHex']!r} is not #RRGGBB")
        if row["from"] > row["to"]:
            problems.append(f"database {row['id']}: years run backwards")
        if row["quota"] and row["to"] - row["from"] != 10:
            problems.append(f"database {row['id']}: a quota database covers ten years")
    return rows


def parse_records(db_id):
    """Every record of one database, read from its Kotlin files."""
    records = []
    for path in sorted(SEED.glob(f"Db{db_id}*.kt")):
        if not re.match(rf"Db{db_id}[A-Z]", path.name):
            continue  # Db1Languages.kt must not pick up Db10Languages.kt
        for block in ENTRY.findall(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            records.append({
                "db": db_id,
                "title": TITLE.search(block).group(1),
                "kind": KIND.search(block).group(1),
                "year": int(YEAR.search(block).group(1)),
                "rare": "rare = true" in block,
                # entry() defaults to database 1 when a record names no databaseId (old records of database 1)
                "database_id": int(DATABASE_ID.search(block).group(1)) if DATABASE_ID.search(block) else 1,
                "runnable": "instructions = " in block,
                "has_example": "example = " in block,
                "text": block,
                "file": path.name,
            })
    return records


def check_database(row, records, problems):
    n = row["id"]
    if not records:
        problems.append(f"database {n}: no records found in the seed folder")
        return
    if row["quota"]:
        for suffix in FILE_SUFFIXES:
            if not (SEED / f"Db{n}{suffix}.kt").exists():
                problems.append(f"database {n}: missing file Db{n}{suffix}.kt")
    if not re.search(rf"val db{n}Records\b", "\n".join(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
                                                       for p in SEED.glob(f"Db{n}*.kt"))):
        problems.append(f"database {n}: no val db{n}Records in its catalogue file")
    for record in records:
        if record["database_id"] != n:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {record['title']!r} has databaseId {record['database_id']}")
    titles = [r["title"] for r in records]
    for title, count in collections.Counter(titles).items():
        if count > 1:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: title {title!r} appears {count} times")
    if not row["quota"]:
        return
    for record in records:
        if record["runnable"] != (record["kind"] in RUNNABLE):
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {record['title']!r} has instructions only if runnable")
        if record["has_example"] != (record["kind"] in RUNNABLE):
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {record['title']!r} has an example only if runnable")
    counts = collections.Counter(r["kind"] for r in records)
    for kind in KINDS:
        if counts[kind] != QUOTA_COUNTS[kind]:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {kind} has {counts[kind]} records, expected {QUOTA_COUNTS[kind]}")
    if len(records) != 50:
        problems.append(f"database {n}: {len(records)} records, expected 50")
    rare = sum(1 for r in records if r["rare"])
    if not 7 <= rare <= 10:
        problems.append(f"database {n}: {rare} rare records, expected 7 to 10")
    for record in records:
        if not row["from"] <= record["year"] <= row["to"]:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {record['title']!r} is dated {record['year']}, "
                            f"outside {row['from']} to {row['to']}")
        for phrase in FORBIDDEN:
            if phrase in record["text"].lower():
                problems.append(f"database {n}: {record['title']!r} contains {phrase!r}")
        if "$" in record["text"]:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {record['title']!r} contains a dollar sign")
        if CYRILLIC.search(record["text"]):
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {record['title']!r} contains Cyrillic")


def check_catalogue(rows, all_records, problems):
    """A title may not appear in two databases; repeats inside one database are checked there."""
    databases_of = collections.defaultdict(set)
    for record in all_records:
        databases_of[record["title"]].add(record["db"])
    for title, owners in databases_of.items():
        if len(owners) > 1 and title not in ALLOWED_DUPLICATE_TITLES:
            problems.append(f"title {title!r} appears in databases {sorted(owners)}")


def wrap_names(names):
    """Joins names with ' + ' into lines of at most 120 characters."""
    lines, current = [], "    "
    for i, name in enumerate(names):
        piece = name + (" + " if i < len(names) - 1 else "")
        if current.strip() and len(current) + len(piece.rstrip()) > 120:
            lines.append(current.rstrip())
            current = "        "
        current += piece
    lines.append(current.rstrip())
    return "\n".join(lines)


def seed_catalog_text(rows):
    entities = []
    for row in rows:
        entities.append(
            "    DatabaseEntity(\n"
            f"        id = {row['id']},\n"
            f'        name = "{row["name"]}",\n'
            f'        description = "{row["description"]}",\n'
            f'        colorHex = "{row["colorHex"]}",\n'
            "    ),\n")
    years = "".join(f"    {r['id']}L to {r['from']}..{r['to']},\n" for r in rows)
    names = [f"db{r['id']}Records" for r in rows]
    return (
        "package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed\n\n"
        "import com.example.retrodatabases.data.DatabaseEntity\n"
        "import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity\n\n"
        "// Generated by tools/build_catalogue.py from tools/databases.json. Do not edit by hand.\n"
        "// To add a database: add its entry to tools/databases.json, write its record files\n"
        "// (databaseId = the new id, one file per kind) and run python3 tools/build_catalogue.py.\n\n"
        f"/** Version of the database file: the number of the newest seeded database. */\n"
        f"const val DATABASE_VERSION = {len(rows)}\n\n"
        "/** The catalogue of databases that are created on the first launch, in id order. */\n"
        "val seedDatabases: List<DatabaseEntity> = listOf(\n"
        + "".join(entities) +
        ")\n\n"
        "/** Years each seeded catalogue covers. The tests check the records against them. */\n"
        "val seedYears: Map<Long, IntRange> = mapOf(\n"
        + years +
        ")\n\n"
        "/** Records of every seeded database. They are inserted together with the databases. */\n"
        "val seedRecords: List<RecordEntity> =\n"
        + wrap_names(names) + "\n"
    )


def sentence_list(items):
    if len(items) <= 1:
        return "".join(items)
    return ", ".join(items[:-1]) + " and " + items[-1]


def catalogue_section(row, records):
    n = row["id"]
    lines = [f"The catalogue of database {n} ({row['from']} to {row['to']}) has the same ten kinds:", "",
             "| Kind | Records | What it is |", "|---|---:|---|"]
    for kind in KINDS:
        titles = [r["title"] for r in records if r["kind"] == kind]
        lines.append(f"| {KIND_LABELS[kind]} | {len(titles)} | {sentence_list(titles)} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def replace_block(text, begin, end, body, path):
    if begin not in text or end not in text:
        sys.exit(f"{path.name}: add the markers {begin!r} and {end!r} once, where the block belongs")
    head, rest = text.split(begin, 1)
    _, tail = rest.split(end, 1)
    return head + begin + "\n" + body + end + tail


def overview_block(rows, by_db):
    coding = [r for r in rows if r.get("group", "coding") == "coding"]
    economics = [r for r in rows if r.get("group") == "economics"]
    total = sum(len(by_db[r["id"]]) for r in rows)
    rare_total = sum(1 for r in rows for x in by_db[r["id"]] if x["rare"])
    lines = [f"Inside are {len(coding)} databases of coding history, from {min(r['from'] for r in coding)} "
             f"to {max(r['to'] for r in coding)}, and {len(economics)} databases of economics: for each part of "
             "society, the best and worst practice of each economic model, and a compromise. The table gives each "
             "one's years, records and rare records. The kinds and titles of every database are in "
             "[CATALOGUE.md](CATALOGUE.md).", "",
             "| Database | Years | Records | Rare |", "|---|---|---:|---:|"]
    for r in rows:
        records = by_db[r["id"]]
        rare = sum(1 for x in records if x["rare"])
        lines.append(f"| {r['id']} | {r['from']} to {r['to']} | {len(records)} | {rare} |")
    lines.append(f"| **All** | | **{total:,}** | **{rare_total}** |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def structure_block(rows):
    last = len(rows)
    return (
        f"- `app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/data` — Room: entities, DAO, converters, the database "
        f"itself, seeding on first launch and one generic migration for each version from 1 to {last} "
        f"(`seedMigrations`).\n"
        f"- `app/src/main/java/com/example/retrodatabases/data/seed` — the records of all {last} databases: "
        f"`Db1*.kt` to `Db{last}*.kt`. The coding databases have one file per kind; each economics database has one "
        f"generated file, `Db<id>Economics.kt`. Also `SeedCatalog.kt`, generated from `tools/databases.json`, and the "
        f"helper that builds a record (`SeedEntry.kt`).\n"
        f"- `tools` — `databases.json` (the databases, their years and colours), `build_catalogue.py`, which "
        f"regenerates `SeedCatalog.kt`, the economics files, the overview in this file and `CATALOGUE.md`, and checks "
        f"every record; and `economics/` (the economic models, the spheres and practices, and one JSON file per "
        f"economics database).\n")


def catalogue_body(rows, by_db):
    sections = []
    for row in rows:
        if row["curated"]:
            continue  # written by hand in CATALOGUE.md, above the generated part
        if row.get("group") == "economics":
            sections.append(economy_catalogue_section(row, by_db[row["id"]]))
        else:
            sections.append(catalogue_section(row, by_db[row["id"]]))
    return "\n".join(sections)


def load_json(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def kotlin_string(text):
    """A Kotlin string literal. The checks refuse dollar signs and line breaks, the two characters that need care here."""
    return '"' + text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'


def economy_records(row, models, spheres, problems):
    """The records of one economics database, built from tools/economics/db<id>.json and the two spec files."""
    n = row["id"]
    path = ECONOMICS / f"db{n}.json"
    if not path.exists():
        problems.append(f"database {n}: missing {path.relative_to(ROOT)}")
        return []
    data = load_json(path)
    records = []

    def add(kind, section, title, original, author, year, summary, details):
        records.append({"db": n, "kind": kind, "section": section, "title": title, "original": original,
                        "author": author, "year": year, "summary": summary, "details": details, "rare": False})

    if data.get("database") != n:
        problems.append(f"database {n}: the file names database {data.get('database')}")
    if data.get("type") == "spheres":
        given = data.get("spheres", [])
        if [item.get("sphere") for item in given] != [s["name"] for s in spheres]:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: the spheres must be the {len(spheres)} names of spheres.json, in order")
        for sphere, item in zip(spheres, given):
            add("COMPROMISE", sphere["name"], f"Compromise: {sphere['name'].lower()}", COMPROMISE_ORIGINAL,
                ECONOMY_AUTHOR, ECONOMY_YEAR, item.get("summary", ""), item.get("details", ""))
        common = data.get("common", {})
        add("COMPROMISE", "All spheres", "Compromise: all spheres", COMPROMISE_ORIGINAL, ECONOMY_AUTHOR,
            ECONOMY_YEAR, common.get("summary", ""), common.get("details", ""))
        return records
    if data.get("type") == "models":
        short = None
    elif data.get("type") == "practice":
        practice = next((p for s in spheres for p in s["practices"] if p["database"] == n), None)
        if practice is None or data.get("practice") != practice["name"]:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: the practice must be the one that spheres.json gives this database")
            return records
        short = practice["short"]
    else:
        problems.append(f"database {n}: unknown type {data.get('type')!r}")
        return records
    given = data.get("models", [])
    if [item.get("model") for item in given] != [m["name"] for m in models]:
        problems.append(f"database {n}: the models must be the {len(models)} names of models.json, in order")
    for model, item in zip(models, given):
        title = model["name"] if short is None else f"{model['name']}: {short}"
        add("MODEL", model["family"], title, model["original"], model["author"], model["year"],
            item.get("best", ""), item.get("worst", ""))
    compromise = data.get("compromise", {})
    title = "Compromise: general principles" if short is None else f"Compromise: {short}"
    add("COMPROMISE", "Compromise", title, COMPROMISE_ORIGINAL, ECONOMY_AUTHOR, ECONOMY_YEAR,
        compromise.get("summary", ""), compromise.get("details", ""))
    return records


def check_economy(row, records, models, spheres, problems):
    n = row["id"]
    kinds = collections.Counter(r["kind"] for r in records)
    if kinds["MODEL"] or not records:
        if kinds["MODEL"] != len(models) or kinds["COMPROMISE"] != 1:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {kinds['MODEL']} model records and {kinds['COMPROMISE']} compromises, "
                            f"expected {len(models)} and 1")
    elif kinds["COMPROMISE"] != len(spheres) + 1:
        problems.append(f"database {n}: {kinds['COMPROMISE']} compromises, expected {len(spheres) + 1}")
    for title, count in collections.Counter(r["title"] for r in records).items():
        if count > 1:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: title {title!r} appears {count} times")
    for record in records:
        title = record["title"]
        text = record["summary"] + " " + record["details"]
        if not row["from"] <= record["year"] <= row["to"]:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {title!r} is dated {record['year']}, outside {row['from']} to {row['to']}")
        for field in ("summary", "details"):
            value = record[field]
            if not value or value != value.strip() or "\n" in value or "  " in value:
                problems.append(f"database {n}: {title!r} has an empty {field}, extra spaces or a line break")
        for phrase in FORBIDDEN:
            if phrase in text.lower():
                problems.append(f"database {n}: {title!r} contains {phrase!r}")
        if "$" in text:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {title!r} contains a dollar sign")
        if CYRILLIC.search(text):
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {title!r} contains Cyrillic")
        low_s, high_s, low_d, high_d = ECONOMY_WORDS[record["kind"]]
        for field, low, high in (("summary", low_s, high_s), ("details", low_d, high_d)):
            count = len(record[field].split())
            if not low <= count <= high:
                problems.append(f"database {n}: {title!r} {field} has {count} words, expected {low} to {high}")
        if "Source:" not in record["details"]:
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {title!r} has no 'Source:' in its details")
        if record["kind"] == "COMPROMISE" and ("Keeps:" not in record["details"] or "Blocks:" not in record["details"]):
            problems.append(f"database {n}: {title!r} must say what it keeps and what it blocks")


def economy_entry(n, record):
    lines = [
        "    entry(",
        f"        databaseId = {n},",
        f"        kind = Kind.{record['kind']},",
        f"        section = {kotlin_string(record['section'])},",
        f"        title = {kotlin_string(record['title'])},",
        f"        originalTitle = {kotlin_string(record['original'])},",
        f"        author = {kotlin_string(record['author'])},",
        f"        year = {record['year']},",
        f"        summary = {kotlin_string(record['summary'])},",
        f"        details = {kotlin_string(record['details'])},",
        "    ),",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def economy_file_text(row, records):
    n = row["id"]
    entries = "\n".join(economy_entry(n, record) for record in records)
    return (
        "package com.example.retrodatabases.data.seed\n\n"
        "import com.example.retrodatabases.data.Kind\n"
        "import com.example.retrodatabases.data.RecordEntity\n\n"
        f"// Generated by tools/build_catalogue.py from tools/economics/db{n}.json. Do not edit by hand.\n\n"
        f"/** {row['description']} */\n"
        f"val db{n}Records: List<RecordEntity> = listOf(\n\n"
        f"{entries})\n"
    )


def economy_catalogue_section(row, records):
    n = row["id"]
    lines = [f"The catalogue of database {n} ({row['from']} to {row['to']}): {row['description']}", "",
             "| Kind | Records | What it is |", "|---|---:|---|"]
    for kind in ECONOMY_KINDS:
        titles = [r["title"] for r in records if r["kind"] == kind]
        if titles:
            lines.append(f"| {KIND_LABELS[kind]} | {len(titles)} | {sentence_list(titles)} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="run the checks only; write nothing")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    problems = []
    rows = load_spec(problems)
    models = load_json(MODELS_SPEC)["models"]
    spheres = load_json(SPHERES_SPEC)["spheres"]
    by_db = {}
    economy_text = {}
    for row in rows:
        if row.get("group") == "economics":
            by_db[row["id"]] = economy_records(row, models, spheres, problems)
            economy_text[row["id"]] = economy_file_text(row, by_db[row["id"]])
        else:
            by_db[row["id"]] = parse_records(row["id"])
    all_records = [r for records in by_db.values() for r in records]
    for row in rows:
        if row.get("group") == "economics":
            check_economy(row, by_db[row["id"]], models, spheres, problems)
            path = SEED / f"Db{row['id']}Economics.kt"
            if args.check and (not path.exists() or path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != economy_text[row["id"]]):
                problems.append(f"database {row['id']}: {path.name} is out of date; run the generator")
        else:
            check_database(row, by_db[row["id"]], problems)
    check_catalogue(rows, all_records, problems)

    if problems:
        print("checks failed:")
        for problem in problems:
            print("  -", problem)
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"checks passed: {len(rows)} databases, {len(all_records)} records")

    if args.check:
        return
    for row in rows:
        if row.get("group") == "economics":
            (SEED / f"Db{row['id']}Economics.kt").write_text(economy_text[row["id"]], encoding="utf-8")
    SEED_CATALOG.write_text(seed_catalog_text(rows), encoding="utf-8")
    CATALOGUE.write_text(replace_block(CATALOGUE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                                       "<!-- BEGIN GENERATED CATALOGUE -->", "<!-- END GENERATED CATALOGUE -->",
                                       catalogue_body(rows, by_db), CATALOGUE), encoding="utf-8")
    text = README.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    text = replace_block(text, "<!-- BEGIN GENERATED OVERVIEW -->", "<!-- END GENERATED OVERVIEW -->",
                         overview_block(rows, by_db), README)
    text = replace_block(text, "<!-- BEGIN GENERATED STRUCTURE -->", "<!-- END GENERATED STRUCTURE -->",
                         structure_block(rows), README)
    README.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    print("wrote SeedCatalog.kt, the economics files, the generated part of CATALOGUE.md and the blocks of README.md")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Test: measure unemployment, output, inflation, shortages, bank failures and inequality in pilot regions against comparison regions, over a full business cycle. Source: Yugoslav pamphlet on self-management; Kornai, Econometrica; Christian Science Monitor, Chile's economy and the Chicago Boys; World Politics, Hungarian economic reform; inferred principles: Ostrom, Van Parijs, Müller-Armack."}

    "summary": "One nine-year common school for every child, paid for by the state with no fees. Parents choose among public schools under admission rules that stop selection by income, forbid tracking at about age ten, and exclude no pupil for any reason.",
    "details": "Keeps: one common school for all pupils (Nordic social democracy, from Finland's comprehensive school reform (peruskoulu)); parental choice among competing schools (Classical laissez-faire capitalism, from Sweden's free-school reform); no fees for compulsory pupils (Chinese market socialism, from China's exemption from charges for rural compulsory education). Blocks: tracking at about age ten (Early tracking in the German school system), safeguarded by common lessons until the common school ends; selection by family income (Chile's school voucher reform), safeguarded by lotteries for oversubscribed places; exclusion of migrant pupils (China's exemption from charges for rural compulsory education), safeguarded by covering every pupil. Test: for about a decade, yearly national test results, the gap between low- and high-income pupils, a segregation index by municipality and the share of pupils on separate tracks, each compared with the year before the reform. Source: IFAU working paper (2006); SNS research brief 7; CESifo working paper 2007; New America, school choice in Chile; US-China Economic and Security Review Commission summaries; China Daily (2006)."

Blocks: fee rises where state funding falls short, blocked by a fully funded cap; lower language scores and costs above returns, blocked by early-learning standards and a cost review (that evidence comes from working papers, and the 2013 study is non-experimental); exclusion of poor families, blocked by a fee-free place for the lowest incomes. Test: places for children aged two to five, fees relative to income, and language at school entry against a comparison group, over the years after each change. Source: Riksdag written question on evaluating the maxtaxa (2004); CIRPEE working paper 08-23 (2008); CIRPEE working paper 13-34 (2013); Living New Deal, The Crisis of Childcare and the profile of Grace Langdon (secondary web sources); Smith, The Wealth of Nations (1776)."
  }

    "details": "Keeps: tax-funded care free at the point of use, from The National Health Service, 1948 (Fabian socialism, Nordic social democracy); one national purchaser covering nearly all people, from Taiwan's national health insurance from 1995 (Developmental state); social insurance for sickness, from Germany's sickness insurance law of 1883 (Social market economy); and a compulsory savings account for health care, from Singapore's MediSave account from 1984 (Monetarist neoliberalism). Blocks: charges added during budget cuts, safeguarded by a parliamentary vote; purchaser favouritism, safeguarded by published prices and an annual independent audit; loss of cover through cuts, safeguarded by a fixed coverage floor; inpatient-heavy care, safeguarded by a ring-fenced primary care budget. Test: coverage share, out-of-pocket share of spending, waiting times and clinic visits, every year from launch. Source: Warwick University Library (secondary); Deutschlandmuseum calendar entry for 1 December 1883; BMC Health Services Research (2010); Dollars and Sense on MediSave (secondary); PubMed Central PMC6220729 (secondary); Johnson (1982) and Harvey (2005), model sources for inferred safeguards."

Blocks: under-assessed land, by yearly revaluation (Pittsburgh's split-rate land tax); VAT leakage, by yearly reconciliation (EU VAT gap, the shortfall against expected VAT); one consumer levy carrying the budget, by a cap on any one tax's share (Turnover tax in the Soviet budget during the war); steep top-rate cuts, by a progressivity review first (US top federal income tax rate, 1913 to 1987). Test: over a full economic cycle, the share of land revalued, the VAT gap, the largest tax's share of revenue and the top rate's progressivity. Source: OECD seminar presentation (2000); Tax Foundation (2024); Law Society Gazette (2024); Oates and Schwab (1997); Higher School of Economics write-up; Wolters Kluwer explainer (2026); Keynes, The General Theory (1936)."

    "details": "Keeps: income security with mandatory participation for claimants, from Nordic social democracy and Denmark's flexicurity model, whose effectiveness point is unconfirmed; short-time work, from Keynesian welfare capitalism and Germany's Kurzarbeit short-time work scheme, whose 'no sign of a causal effect' is not proof of no effect; a floor paid without a job-search test, from Universal basic income and Finland's basic income trial for unemployed people, whose results are preliminary. Blocks: easy dismissal with thin income support, from Monetarist neoliberalism, safeguarded by earnings-related benefits and the floor; hidden unemployment, from Command socialism, safeguarded by published counts of jobless and underemployed people. Test: for two years after a job loss, compare job-finding and pay on re-employment between the two routes, using register data, and track hours against headcount in short-time schemes.
